_schema: Each rule: name, scopeGlob (regex applied to repo-relative path), excludeGlob (optional), principle (free-form reference), prompt (template — {{content}} substitutes file content), maxFiles (per-rule cap to control cost), severity (warn|error)

rules.name: top-bar-reimplementation
rules.principle: intent/ui.md — top bars should be a shared component, not reimplemented per screen. PRINCIPLES § VIII.25 — code wins; if the screen does its own top bar, that's drift from intent.

rules.name: uses-design-tokens
rules.principle: intent/ui.md — ALL colors come from design-tokens.ts. PRINCIPLES § VIII.25.

rules.name: file-matches-intent
rules.principle: .cipher/layer2/intent-index.json — every file has a recorded 2-sentence intent. PRINCIPLES § VIII.25 — code wins, but if code drifts past its declared intent, that's a signal the intent (or the code) is stale.

rules.name: screen-anti-slop
rules.principle: intent/ui.md anti-slop rules: (1) one focal point, (2) visual hierarchy (size+weight+color contrast for different info levels), (3) structured cards (header row + content + metadata, not just text), (4) interactive feedback on pressables (scale/opacity).
rules.prompt:
You are auditing a React Native screen against Ozzu's anti-slop UI rules.

ANTI-SLOP RULES:
1. ONE FOCAL POINT — the screen shouldn't compete with itself; one primary action or content area dominates.
2. VISUAL HIERARCHY — title/subtitle/metadata must differ in size + weight + color (not all the same fontSize/color/weight).
3. CARDS HAVE STRUCTURE — cards are NOT 'text on a slightly different background'. A card has: container (bg + border or accent), header row (icon + title + status), content (description, progress), metadata row (pills, timestamps).
4. PRESSABLE FEEDBACK — Pressables/Buttons need opacity change OR scale animation on press (e.g., transform:[{scale:0.98}], opacity:0.92).

FILE: {{path}}

```tsx
{{content}}
```

Which of these four rules does this screen visibly violate? Reply with strict JSON only:

{"violates": true|false, "reason": "<which numbered rules are violated, one sentence each>"}
